intro: My research develops statistical tools for analysing time series whose behaviour changes over time. The applied questions are often in finance and in the sciences, where regime changes, shocks and non-stationarity are the central difficulty.

current.title: Spectral estimation for non-stationary time series
current.status: PhD research in progress, University of Bath, SAMBa Centre for Doctoral Training. Supervisor: Matthew Nunes.
current.summary: I am currently investigating estimates of spectral quantities for non-stationary time series, i.e. time series whose structure changes with time. I will also implement useful packages for calculating these in Python.

background.title: Near-critical percolation and branching processes
background.status: Where I began my PhD, before switching my focus to time series.
background.summary: I began my doctoral research in near-critical percolation and branching processes, two areas of probability theory about random structures and their critical behaviour. I then switched my focus to non-stationary time series.
